prompt.brief: Design Twitter for millions of users: people can publish short posts, follow accounts, read a home timeline, and see new posts appear without overwhelming the system when popular users publish.
successSignals: Separate the durable post and follow graph from the read-optimized home timeline projection.
Choose a fanout strategy based on follower count and make celebrity posts safe for hot keys and burst traffic.
Define cursor pagination, ordering, deletion, privacy, and idempotency instead of treating the feed as an unbounded list.
Keep media processing, search, analytics, and notifications asynchronous so timeline reads and writes remain predictable.

functional: Allow authenticated users to publish, delete, and read short text posts with optional media references.
Allow users to follow and unfollow accounts, then read a reverse-chronological home timeline.
Show a user's profile timeline and a post detail view with replies, reposts, and likes as extensible interactions.
Refresh the home timeline and notify clients when new posts are available, subject to visibility and moderation rules.
nonFunctional: Target p95 under 200 ms for a timeline page read and under 150 ms for publishing metadata before asynchronous work.
A committed post must be durable and eventually visible to eligible followers; brief feed lag is acceptable and observable.
Support privacy, blocked users, deleted content, abuse controls, rate limits, and authenticated access at every read path.
Remain available during celebrity-post bursts, regional failures, slow media processing, and partial fanout backlog.
scaleAssumptions: 500 million registered users, 100 million daily active users, and 50 million posts per day.
Assume 20 timeline reads per daily active user and 10x traffic bursts around major events.
Most users follow fewer than 1,000 accounts; a small set of accounts has tens of millions of followers.
Keep post metadata in a durable partitioned store, media in object storage, and feed entries as rebuildable projections with a retention window.

metrics.label: Post rate
metrics.description: 50M daily posts with burst capacity for live events and retry storms.

metrics.label: Timeline reads
metrics.description: 100M daily users at 20 reads each; cache and precomputed entries absorb hot reads.

metrics.label: Read latency
metrics.description: Fetch a bounded page by cursor without scanning the entire follow graph.

metrics.label: Feed freshness
metrics.description: Normal fanout target; show a refresh affordance when stream or projection lag grows.

entities.name: Post
entities.notes: The post store is the durable source of truth; immutable content plus moderation state makes fanout and deletion repairable.

entities.name: FollowEdge
entities.notes: Maintain follower and following access paths so writes can find recipients and profile reads can list relationships efficiently.

entities.name: TimelineEntry
entities.notes: A read-optimized, rebuildable projection. Store bounded windows and merge with a pull path for high-follower accounts.

entities.name: FeedEvent
entities.notes: Partition by author or post for ordered publication events; consumers deduplicate and can replay after failures.

apis.contract: { text, mediaIds?, visibility, requestId } -> { postId, createdAt }
apis.notes: Authenticate, validate length and media ownership, persist the post idempotently, then enqueue publication and indexing work.
Read a bounded page from the user's feed projection, merge eligible pull sources when needed, and filter deleted or blocked content.
Authorize the actor and conditionally create the edge; follow changes affect future fanout and can trigger a bounded backfill policy.
Make unfollow idempotent and remove or tombstone future entries without requiring a full feed rewrite.
Authorize subscription and send a snapshot or resync marker after reconnect or an event-version gap.

dataFlow.title: Accept the post
dataFlow.description: The edge authenticates the author, validates content and visibility, and the post service writes durable metadata with a client request ID.

dataFlow.title: Publish the post event
dataFlow.description: A transactional outbox or change stream emits one ordered FeedEvent after the post commit; the API acknowledges without waiting for every follower.

dataFlow.title: Choose a fanout strategy
dataFlow.description: The fanout service looks up the author's follower count and sends normal authors to push fanout while celebrity authors use pull-on-read or hybrid delivery.

dataFlow.title: Build the home timeline
dataFlow.description: Workers write idempotent TimelineEntry records to recipient partitions, apply visibility and block rules, and expire entries outside the feed window.

dataFlow.title: Read and refresh asynchronously
dataFlow.description: The timeline API merges a bounded projection with hot-author pull results, returns a cursor and lag metadata, and a live gateway coalesces new-post notifications.

architecture.title: Twitter-style home timeline reference architecture
architecture.summary: Durable posts and follow edges feed a hybrid timeline pipeline: push fanout serves ordinary accounts, while pull-on-read protects the system from celebrity fanout explosions.

layers.label: Experience layer
layers.description: Clients publish posts, read cursor-paginated feeds, and receive freshness-aware refresh events.

layers.label: Source and control plane
layers.description: Post and graph services own durable content, relationships, authorization, and moderation state.

layers.label: Feed and event plane
layers.description: Events are partitioned, fanout is hybrid, and timeline projections are independently rebuilt and cached.

layers.label: Asynchronous extensions
layers.description: Media, search, notifications, analytics, and repair consume events without blocking the core feed path.

keyPaths.label: Publish path
keyPaths.description: Client -> edge -> post service -> durable post store -> event stream.

keyPaths.label: Home timeline path
keyPaths.description: Timeline request -> cache/store, merged with hot-author pull results and visibility checks.

keyPaths.label: Hybrid fanout path
keyPaths.description: Feed event -> strategy -> push projection or pull-on-read for high-follower authors.

components.label: Web and mobile clients
components.description: Publish posts, request bounded feed pages, and subscribe for new-post notifications.

components.label: Edge gateway
components.description: Terminates TLS, authenticates users, applies quotas, and routes by user or post key.

components.label: Post service
components.description: Validates, authorizes, stores, and deletes posts while emitting durable publication events.

components.label: Post store
components.description: Partitioned durable source of truth for post metadata, visibility, and moderation state.

components.label: Social graph service
components.description: Manages follow edges, blocks, privacy, and recipient lookups with versioned changes.

components.label: Follow graph
components.description: Durable adjacency lists optimized for follower enumeration and relationship checks.

components.label: Feed event stream
components.description: Retained, partitioned events for fanout, indexing, notifications, analytics, and replay.

components.label: Hybrid fanout service
components.description: Chooses push, pull, or hybrid delivery from follower count, backlog, and account policy.

components.label: Timeline projections
components.description: Sharded, rebuildable feed entries keyed by recipient with cursor-friendly rank keys.

components.label: Feed cache
components.description: Caches recent pages and post summaries with version or lag metadata to absorb read bursts.

components.label: Timeline service
components.description: Reads projections, merges pull sources for hot authors, filters visibility, and creates opaque cursors.

components.label: Live update gateway
components.description: Tracks feed subscribers and coalesces new-post notifications; clients fetch the authoritative page on refresh.

components.label: Media pipeline
components.description: Scans, resizes, and publishes media through object storage and a CDN without blocking post metadata.

components.label: Search index
components.description: Indexes eligible posts and accounts asynchronously for discovery and search queries.

components.label: Notification service
components.description: Delivers mentions, follows, and selected post notifications with dedupe and provider retries.

components.label: Analytics and abuse
components.description: Consumes events for trends, ranking signals, abuse detection, and product reporting.

components.label: Observability
components.description: Tracks feed lag, fanout backlog, cache hit rate, hot partitions, read latency, and projection drift.

connections.label: Publish / read
connections.description: Authenticated API requests for posts, graph actions, and timeline pages.

connections.label: Post command
connections.description: Routes validated post commands to the owning service.

connections.label: Durable post
connections.description: Commits content and visibility state before downstream fanout.

connections.label: Follow command
connections.description: Creates or removes a versioned follow edge.

connections.label: Graph edge
connections.description: Maintains both follower and following access patterns.

connections.label: FeedEvent
connections.description: Emits the committed post transition for independent consumers.

connections.label: Graph change
connections.description: Publishes follow, unfollow, block, and privacy changes.

connections.label: Publication event
connections.description: Fanout strategy is selected using follower cardinality and backlog.

connections.label: Recipients
connections.description: Enumerates bounded recipient batches for push fanout.

connections.label: TimelineEntry
connections.description: Writes idempotent entries for ordinary authors and hybrid paths.

connections.label: Recent pages
connections.description: Warms or invalidates bounded recent feed pages.

connections.label: Cursor read
connections.description: Routes the user's home timeline request.

connections.label: Cached snapshot
connections.description: Serves recent pages while preserving freshness metadata.

connections.label: Projection read
connections.description: Fetches entries by recipient and rank cursor.

connections.label: Hot-author pull
connections.description: Merges recent posts from pull sources and rechecks visibility.

connections.label: New-post hint
connections.description: Signals that a later cursor read can fetch newer items.

connections.label: Refresh event
connections.description: Coalesced notification; the feed API remains authoritative.

connections.label: Media job
connections.description: Processes media asynchronously and updates its readiness state.

connections.label: Index event
connections.description: Indexes eligible content without delaying publication.

connections.label: Notification event
connections.description: Delivers selected notifications with retries and dedupe.

connections.label: Analytics event
connections.description: Feeds ranking, reporting, and abuse systems off the critical path.

connections.label: Lag metrics
connections.description: Observes consumer lag, partition pressure, and replay health.

deepDives.title: Fanout-on-write, fanout-on-read, or hybrid
points: Push entries for ordinary accounts because most users benefit from a cheap bounded read.
Pull recent posts for celebrity accounts because writing to tens of millions of recipient partitions per post creates a hot fanout event.
Use a threshold and hybrid merge in the timeline service; make the strategy observable and adjustable rather than embedding a permanent follower-count constant.

deepDives.title: Timeline storage and pagination
points: Key projections by recipient and use a stable rank key combining event time with a tie-breaker, so pagination does not skip or duplicate posts.
Return opaque cursors containing the last rank and strategy version; do not use page numbers over a changing feed.
Keep a bounded window and rebuild entries from posts, graph changes, and visibility state when projections expire or drift.

deepDives.title: Hot posts, bursts, and live updates
points: Partition large recipient writes, rate-limit fanout workers, and isolate celebrity work queues from normal authors.
The live channel sends a refresh hint or newest sequence rather than the full feed; clients fetch authoritative data through the normal cursor API.
Monitor event lag and feed freshness, then degrade to pull reads or a stale-marked feed when push delivery is overloaded.

deepDives.title: Privacy, deletion, and ranking evolution
points: Apply visibility, block, mute, and moderation checks during both fanout and read-time merge because policies can change after an entry is written.
Delete or tombstone source posts and invalidate projections; a feed entry must never be treated as the canonical content.
Keep the event stream and projection versioned so ranking experiments can create a new projection without rewriting the source data model.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull fanout
tradeoffs.recommendation: Use hybrid fanout: push for normal accounts and pull for high-follower accounts, with a configurable threshold and bounded merge.
tradeoffs.caution: Pure push amplifies celebrity writes; pure pull makes every timeline read traverse the graph and increases tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Freshness versus read cost
tradeoffs.recommendation: Precompute a recent feed window and send coalesced refresh hints, accepting seconds of projection lag with visible metrics.
tradeoffs.caution: Synchronous fanout cannot meet burst availability goals, while an unmarked stale cache creates confusing product behavior.

tradeoffs.title: Chronological versus ranked timeline
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start reverse chronological for explainability, but keep rank_key and projection versions flexible for later ranking signals.
tradeoffs.caution: Ranking adds feature-store, experimentation, and consistency complexity; it should not obscure the core feed access pattern.

commonMistakes: Writing one timeline row synchronously for every follower before acknowledging a post.
Using a single list per user without partitioning, bounded retention, or repair semantics.
Ignoring celebrity accounts, burst traffic, cache stampedes, and fanout backlog isolation.
Using offset pagination over a changing feed instead of a stable cursor and tie-breaker.
Trusting cached feed entries after a post is deleted or a privacy/block relationship changes.

followUps.question: How would you add replies and threaded conversations?
followUps.answer: Keep posts immutable with parent_id and conversation_id indexes, then build bounded reply pages and asynchronous counters; do not make the home timeline traverse an entire thread.

followUps.question: How would you add personalized ranking?
followUps.answer: Keep the source post and follow graph unchanged, add a versioned candidate and ranking stage, and materialize ranked windows only where latency and traffic justify it.

followUps.question: What happens when a user follows an account?
followUps.answer: Write the edge immediately, then asynchronously backfill a bounded number of recent eligible posts; the read path can merge the followee's newest posts while backfill catches up.

followUps.question: How do you rebuild a damaged timeline?
followUps.answer: Replay retained post, graph, moderation, and deletion events into a shadow projection for selected users, compare versions and counts, then switch or repair partitions incrementally.

rubric.description: The answer identifies durable posts and graph edges separately from rebuildable recipient timeline projections.
The design explains hybrid push/pull behavior, celebrity thresholds, partitioning, backpressure, and burst isolation.
Timeline reads are bounded, cursor-paginated, cacheable, visibility-aware, and explicit about freshness and lag.
Idempotent events, replay, projection repair, deletion handling, and degraded pull behavior protect against partial failure.
Authentication, privacy, blocks, moderation, rate limits, abuse controls, and asynchronous extensions are part of the architecture.
